findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads "So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?" and "Download", at both widths
findings.fault: The subheads use a heavy, wide, black-weight grotesque. That makes it a third typeface, and it belongs to neither half of the stated pair. The type-pair panel promises Newsreader 500 for subheads. Instead, every subhead shouts in a squat display sans between the quiet serif body and the light serif headline. This is the one place the specimen is meant to show how Angélique's added subheads will look, and they look like a different, louder site.
findings.who_objects: The founder asked for serious, refined type and for nothing that reads as 'in-your-face techy', and this face feels both blunt and techy. Angélique would also object, because she will add these subheads to every article and they don't match the system the tile describes. A development-bank reader sees a legal journal interrupted by poster type.

findings.where: Article specimen: the title "The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law", compared with Mark's hero line on the first screen
findings.fault: The article title is set in a heavy bold serif, larger and darker than the light hero line. The type pair names only Light 300 for display and 500 for subheads. So the two biggest lines on the site disagree in weight: the homepage is light and refined, while every article opens with a dense, heavy title that loses the tile's main typographic idea.
findings.who_objects: The founder will judge whether the look carries from the homepage into the articles, which the brief calls the product. A heavy title makes the article page feel like a different, more generic publication than the light, personal homepage.

findings.where: Article specimen title, "World's", and the closing body paragraph, "world's best PPP law"
findings.fault: These use a straight typewriter apostrophe, while the quotes and other apostrophes around them are typographic curly marks. At display size the straight tick in the title is easy to see.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader of a legal-journal style page would notice the mismatched punctuation. It weakens the 'well-set brief' polish that Counsel's paper depends on.
